record.paper_title: The Future of Primordial Black Holes: Open Questions and Roadmap
record.original_question: Can PBHs populate the pair-instability mass gap, the predicted deficit of astrophysical black holes between roughly 50 and 120 solar masses caused by pair-instability supernovae, and would a feature in the black-hole mass spectrum reveal a new black-hole formation mechanism?

evidence.quote: An equally powerful mass challenge for PBH arises from the pair instability gap. This is generated by the catastrophic core collapse of massive stars that results from pair-instability SNe, and predicts a deficit of astrophysical BH between∼ 50M⊙ and∼ 120M⊙.
Could PBH populate the pair instability gap? A smoking gun signature would be a feature in the BH mass spectrum, most likely indicative of a new formation mechanism.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Stellar evolution theory predicts that massive stars whose helium cores enter the pair-instability regime either undergo pulsational mass loss or are completely disrupted by pair-instability supernovae, producing a deficit (the "pair-instability mass gap") of stellar-origin black holes with masses roughly between 50 M_⊙ and 120 M_⊙. Primordial black holes (PBHs), defined as black holes formed in the early Universe from the gravitational collapse of cosmological overdensities (rather than from stellar collapse), are not subject to this stellar-evolution constraint and may in principle have any mass.

Let f_PBH(M) denote the differential mass function of a PBH population and let p_obs(M_1, M_2) denote the observed distribution of component masses in merging binary black holes inferred from gravitational-wave catalogs.

(a) Determine whether there exist physically motivated PBH formation scenarios (specifying the curvature power spectrum, equation-of-state features at QCD-like thermal transitions, or other production mechanisms) which yield a PBH abundance and mass spectrum f_PBH(M) such that mergers of PBH binaries can account for a statistically significant fraction of observed binary-black-hole events with at least one component mass in the interval [50 M_⊙, 120 M_⊙], while remaining consistent with all current cosmological, microlensing, CMB, and gravitational-wave constraints on PBHs.

(b) Identify a distinguishing feature in the binary-black-hole mass spectrum (e.g., a peak, edge, or excess inside the pair-instability gap) whose presence would constitute a "smoking-gun" indication of a non-stellar (in particular primordial) black-hole formation channel, and quantify the statistical sensitivity required to establish such a feature.
artifact.category_tag: Primordial black holes and gravitational-wave astronomy
artifact.status_search_result: The question remains open. Recent analyses of LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA GWTC-4 data report evidence of a pair-instability gap in the secondary-mass distribution with a lower edge near ~44 M_⊙, but a number of observed events still have components in or near the gap, and proposals that PBHs (often with thermal/QCD-induced features in the mass function) can populate it are actively studied. No consensus has been reached that PBHs are required or excluded as the explanation, and the proposed smoking-gun spectral feature has not been definitively identified.

status_evidence.title: Evidence of the pair-instability gap from black-hole masses (Nature)
status_evidence.snippet: Analysis of GWTC-4 finds a deficit of secondary BH masses with a lower edge around 44 M_⊙, consistent with pair-instability predictions.
status_evidence.claim: Observational evidence for the gap exists but the origin of in-gap events is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Primordial black hole mass function with mass gap (MNRAS)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs PBH mass functions that can populate the pair-instability mass gap.
status_evidence.claim: PBH scenarios capable of populating the gap continue to be actively proposed.

status_evidence.title: The Pair-instability Mass Gap for Black Holes (ApJL 2103.07933)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews uncertainties in the boundaries of the pair-instability mass gap.
status_evidence.claim: The exact extent of the gap remains theoretically uncertain.
